pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Maine Journeyman Electrician examination is administered by Prov for approved candidates through the State of Maine Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation. The exam is computer-based and is offered at approved Prov testing locations. Candidates schedule their exam after receiving the required approval and testing information. The Maine Journeyman Electrician exam includes 80 questions and allows 3 hours of testing time. The exam is designed to test a candidate’s knowledge of the planning, installation, repair, alteration, and maintenance of electrical conductors, raceways, and equipment used for light, heat, and power while employed by a Master Electrician. The Maine Journeyman Electrician exam content outline includes general electrical theory and principles, wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, motors and controls, equipment for general use, special occupancies, special equipment, special conditions, and communication systems.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Wiring and protection and wiring methods and materials are two of the largest listed exam areas, so candidates should give strong attention to NEC structure, installation rules, conductors, overcurrent protection, raceways, boxes, grounding and bonding concepts, equipment requirements, and practical application. The subject breakdown includes 10 questions on general electrical theory and principles, 16 questions on wiring and protection, 16 questions on wiring methods and materials, 10 questions on motors and controls, 10 questions on equipment for general use, 5 questions on special occupancies, 5 questions on special equipment, 5 questions on special conditions, and 3 questions on communication systems. This Ultimate Combo is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code. Candidates should use the included materials to build code familiarity, strengthen trade knowledge, improve calculation skills, and practice exam-style questions.

pieces.t: Official exam references and code editions are controlled by the state and testing provider, so candidates should follow the instructions issued for the exam they are scheduled to take.

pieces.h: Closed Book Test
pieces.t: The Maine electrician examinations are delivered in closed book format unless the candidate information specifically marks a reference as permitted. For the Maine Journeyman Electrician exam, candidates should prepare as though they will not have personal books, study guides, loose notes, or code references available in the testing room unless the official exam instructions for their appointment state otherwise. Closed book testing makes preparation especially important. Candidates need to understand the structure of the National Electrical Code, remember key concepts, recognize common code applications, and practice enough calculations to work confidently without relying on live reference lookup during the exam. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is still an important study tool. Even when the official exam is closed book, studying with the NEC helps candidates learn how code rules are organized, how terms are used, where major electrical topics are located, and how article language connects to real electrical installations.

pieces.h: Closed Book Test
pieces.t: Code-navigation practice during study can improve comprehension, even when the book is not used during the exam itself. Candidates should use study sessions to build memory, understanding, and problem-solving ability. Instead of only looking up answers, candidates should review why the rule applies, what the important terms mean, and how the same concept may be tested in different ways. This approach supports stronger performance on a closed book exam because the candidate is preparing to understand the material, not simply search for it.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Maine journeyman electrician licensing is handled through the Electricians’ Examining Board within the Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation. Candidates must meet the Board’s licensing requirements, complete the required training and experience pathway, pass the journeyman examination, and submit the required application materials for licensure. A typical Maine journeyman electrician path includes working as a licensed apprentice or helper, completing the required electrical education or approved program of study, completing required National Electrical Code coursework, gaining qualifying electrical installation experience under proper supervision, applying through the Board process, taking and passing the journeyman electrician examination, and completing the remaining license application steps. Maine has multiple pathways that may qualify a candidate for the journeyman examination and license.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: These pathways can include completion of an approved apprenticeship program, completion of required classroom study, graduation from certain accredited electrical programs, or other education and experience combinations recognized by the Board. Candidates should keep accurate records of apprentice or helper licensure, employment dates, supervising license information, electrical installation experience, classroom training, apprenticeship completion, NEC coursework, and any certificates or transcripts required by the Board. Organized documentation can make the application process smoother and help avoid delays.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Maine issues statewide electrician licenses through the Electricians’ Examining Board. A Journeyman Electrician is a licensed individual who makes electrical installations in the employment of a Master Electrician, Limited Electrician, or Electrical Company. The license is an individual trade license and is separate from operating as an electrical contractor or business. One Maine journeyman electrician pathway includes completing at least 8,000 hours of service as a licensed apprentice or helper and satisfactorily completing a program of study consisting of 576 hours approved by the Board or from an accredited institution. Required study includes 45-hour courses in Electricity I, Electricity II, Math I, Controls I, and a current National Electrical Code course, along with approved elective study.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Maine also recognizes pathways involving graduation from an accredited applied technology high school two-year electrical program with 7,000 hours of qualifying electrical installation experience and a current National Electrical Code course, or graduation from a Maine community college electrical program or Department of Corrections vocational-electrical program with 4,000 hours of qualifying experience and a current National Electrical Code course. A licensed apprentice who has completed an approved apprenticeship program of study and has worked at least 4,000 hours as a licensed apprentice electrician may qualify to sit for the journeyman examination. Candidates should make sure their education, hours, supervision, and documentation match the pathway they are using. Passing the exam is one part of the Maine journeyman electrician licensing process. Candidates must still satisfy the Board’s licensing requirements, provide the required documentation, and receive license approval from the state.

Even when the test itself is closed book, studying directly from the NEC helps candidates understand how code rules are written, where topics are located, how tables are used, and how exceptions affect final answers.

pieces.h: Closed Book Test
pieces.t: Tabs make study sessions more organized by helping you move between major NEC areas while reviewing practice questions and explanations. The flash cards are especially useful for closed book preparation because they help reinforce memory through repetition. Candidates can use flash cards to review terms, formulas, code concepts, and quick-reference knowledge in short sessions. The Electrician Calculations Study Guide also supports closed book readiness by helping candidates practice solving problems step by step without depending on last-minute lookup.

pieces.h: Q: Is this combo based on the 2026 NEC?
pieces.t: Yes. This combo is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and includes the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback.

pieces.h: Q: What books are included in this package?
pieces.t: This package includes the 2026 Maine Master Electrician Study Guide, the 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide, and the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback.

pieces.h: Q: Who should use this Maine master electrician combo?
pieces.t: This combo is intended for electricians preparing for Maine master electrician exam content, NEC-based questions, open-book code navigation, and electrical calculation problems.

pieces.h: Q: How many questions are on the Maine Master Electrician exam?
pieces.t: The Maine Master Electrician exam includes 100 questions.

pieces.h: Q: How much time is allowed for the Maine Master Electrician exam?
pieces.t: The Maine Master Electrician exam allows 4 hours of testing time.

pieces.h: Q: Who provides the Maine electrician licensing examinations?
pieces.t: Maine has contracted with Prov, Inc. to provide examinations for approved candidates in the state professional licensing examination program.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package help with electrical calculations?
pieces.t: Yes. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is included to help candidates practice formulas, NEC table use, load calculations, conductor sizing, box fill, raceway fill, and other calculation-based topics.

pieces.h: Q: Can I study directly from the NEC with this package?
pieces.t: Yes. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback is included so candidates can study article language, definitions, tables, exceptions, and code requirements directly.

pieces.h: Q: Who is this Maine Master Electrician exam prep combo for?
pieces.t: This combo is for electricians preparing for the Maine Master Electrician exam who want a study guide, flash cards, 12 practice exams, and 2 full final exams in one structured preparation package.

pieces.h: Q: Is this product based on the 2026 National Electrical Code?
pieces.t: Yes. This product is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and is designed to support current NEC-focused exam preparation.

pieces.h: Q: Does this product include practice exams?
pieces.t: Yes. This package includes 12 practice exams plus 2 full final exams. The practice exams help you build familiarity with exam-style questions, and the final exams help you evaluate readiness after completing more of your study plan.

pieces.h: Q: Are flash cards included?
pieces.t: Yes. This is a study guide and flash card combo. The flash cards are designed to help reinforce electrical terms, formulas, trade knowledge, code concepts, and exam-style recall.

pieces.h: Q: What subjects are covered on the Maine Master Electrician exam?
pieces.t: The exam covers general electrical knowledge, communication systems, equipment for general use, service feeders and branch circuits, motors and controls, special conditions, special equipment, special occupancies, wiring and protection, and wiring methods and materials.

pieces.h: Q: Do I need approval before scheduling the Maine Master Electrician exam?
pieces.t: Yes. Candidates must submit an examination application to the Maine Electricians’ Examining Board and receive approval before scheduling the exam with Prov.

pieces.h: Q: What experience is required for the Maine Master Electrician examination pathway?
pieces.t: Maine requires at least 4,000 hours of service as a journeyman electrician or at least 12,000 hours of experience in electrical installations, along with completion of the required 576-hour program of study.

pieces.h: Q: Does this combo guarantee that I will pass the exam?
pieces.t: No. This product is designed to support preparation through structured study, practice exams, final exams, and flash card review. Exam results and licensing approval depend on the candidate’s preparation, testing performance, and state licensing requirements.
